lessons_control.note: pre_lessons is each hunter's own sum before it read researcher_us/LESSONS.md. edge_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, which is the only thing that can tell the guidance file apart from a habit.

language_control.note: RETIRED 2026-09-22: the European and Canadian hunters now run one bilingual pass and emit no freeze, so this is 0/0 on every run sealed after that date. On earlier runs pre_local is each hunter's own sum after the ENGLISH pass and before the local pass; eu_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, per market, and does not pool the UK (where the second pass varied source locality) with Germany and France (where it varied language).

note: Ranked on impact_sum: the hunters' signed per-finding sizes, added up, in points of spot. No call and no threshold -- cut wherever you like afterwards, which is what keeps the ranking question answerable at every k. `conviction` (abs of the key) is where the direction skill lives: over all events the sign is a coin flip, above the median conviction it is 74%. conviction_floor is a floor on emphasis in the note, never a filter on this file. Everything under `diagnostics` was measured as neutral or subtractive and decides nothing -- see researcher_us/EDGE_ANALYSIS.md.

findings.finding: Q3 2026 was storm-free in Florida. No named storm made Florida landfall July-September (Bertha and Edouard hit LA/TX, and the first hurricane of the season, Isaias, came on Oct 9). It was also the first full quarter of the 2026-27 cat program, which Slide says carries a double-digit risk-adjusted rate cut. Peer Universal (UVE), reporting 2026-10-22, showed Q3 net income +31.8% to $52.5M, net loss ratio -5.6 pts to 64.6% and ceded premium ratio 27.6% vs 32.7%. Slide's Q3 2025 analogue earned $111M at a 48.5% CR with a smaller book; Q2 2026 earned $134.9M (EPS $1.06). A Q3 2026 EPS of about $1.10-1.30 against the $0.84 bar is likely. With $274.4M of H1 net income against a $455-470M FY guide that implies only $181-196M for all of H2, a clean Q3 makes a raise to the FY net-income guide near-mechanical.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: SLDE has beaten EPS consensus 5 of 5 times by $0.16-0.36 (MarketBeat table). Reactions: Q2'25 -9.14%, Q3'25 -1.07% (+$0.30 beat), Q4'25 +9.68% (+$0.36 beat with the first FY2026 guide), Q1'26 -2.44% (+$0.20), Q2'26 +3.46% (+$0.18, guide only reaffirmed). Peer UVE beat ~$1.08 consensus by a wide margin on 2026-10-22 and closed +0.91% on 10-23 (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/uve/history/). The one large up-move followed a guidance event.

findings.finding: Hurricane Isaias (Cat 2, Destin, 2026-10-09) is a Q4 loss event that management will likely size on the Oct 28 8:30 ET call. Florida OIR puts statewide insured losses at $582M and 46,509 claims as of Oct 15, 79% in Santa Rosa and Escambia. AM Best calls it an 'earnings event'. UVE's CEO said claims were 'less significant than initially anticipated'. Slide does not report to OIR market-intelligence data, so its own count is unknown. Its retention is $166.8M first event, so any loss is fully net and offsets part of a guide raise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior post-IPO hurricane disclosure for Slide. The stock moved -0.63% on 2026-10-09, landfall day, and has since risen ~14%.

findings.finding: Top-line momentum is fading. Policies in force were flat sequentially (508,928 at Q1 to 509,075 at Q2) as Citizens takeouts slowed to bind reinsurance. Average premium per residential policy fell to $3,614 from $3,964 y/y. Citizens itself had shrunk to ~274k policies by June 2026, so the takeout pool that drove Q4'25 GPW +56.7% is nearly exhausted. Florida's 30-day average homeowners rate request is -4.8%. Q3 GPW is therefore likely flat to down against Q3'25's $463.4M. This lands largely inside the GWP guide of $1.85-1.95B, which against H1's $922.8M implies H2 of $927M-1.03B versus $1.08B in H2'25, down 5-14%. It is a risk for any 2027 growth commentary.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2'25 (-9.14%) and Q3'25 (-1.07%) both missed revenue estimates ($261.6M vs $271.2M; $265.7M vs $279.4M) while beating EPS. Q2'26 beat revenue ($386.8M vs $370.8M) and rose +3.46%.

Short interest rose from 6.45M (Aug 31) to 7.41M shares (Oct 15, 5.9 days to cover, ~10-11% of float). Peer UVE's clean beat bought only +0.9%. findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After a +11.6% run between Q1 and Q2 (per unusualwhales as of Oct 6, for the period since the last print), Q2's beat bought +3.46%. The Q1'26 beat was sold at -2.44%.

H1 buybacks were about $191M, at ~$17.75-17.95 a share, and the initial dividend is $0.07. Debt-to-cap is 2.4%, and a storm-free Q3 adds ~$130-150M of earnings. A new authorization or a dividend step-up is plausible but not announced.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The dividend initiation with Q2 coincided with +3.46%. There is no separate history.

outside_window.finding: The 2027 reinsurance renewal (June 1, 2027) and geographic diversification (NJ, RI, NY launch, California E&S) are framed by management as a 2027 story. No resolution inside the window beyond call commentary.

findings.finding: Costa Rican colón strength continued through Q3: the BCCR reference was about ₡445-454/$ in September 2026 against roughly ₡497 at the start of the year. DMC's Q2 release and Dole's Q2 both cite the colón as a gross-profit headwind, because Costa Rica is the main cost base for DMC's bananas and pineapples.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean isolated reaction. The colón was cited in Q2 2026 (stock +3.79% on an EPS beat), so the market has not punished this line on its own.

findings.finding: The banana segment has an easy comparison and supportive peer pricing. Q3 2025 banana gross profit was only $4.6M (1.3% margin). DMC closed four low-profitability Costa Rican banana farms (a $10.6M Q2 charge). Dole's Q2 (2026-08-10, after DMC spoke) said underlying North American banana pricing was slightly higher and that contractual pricing mechanisms should help in H2. The offset is weak NA banana volumes, which both companies report.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The banana margin collapse drove the -9.78% pre-market move on Q3 2025. In Q2 2026, banana GP fell to $8.4M from $30.0M y/y and the stock still rose 3.79% on the EPS beat.

findings.finding: Avocado selling prices stayed down. Mission Produce, reporting on 2026-09-08 for May-July, saw per-unit avocado prices fall 9% on higher Mexican supply, and guided industry volumes up about 10% y/y for Aug-Oct. DMC already cited lower avocado prices in its Q2 fresh and value-added segment, so the pressure persisted through DMC's Q3. Net of the rest of the company: avocados are part of the $569M F&VA segment, alongside pineapple, fresh-cut and prepared items.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 revenue missed consensus by about 7.5% ($1.219B vs $1.318B), partly on F&VA, and the stock still rose 3.79%: this name has not been punished for revenue misses when EPS beat.

findings.finding: Costa Rican pineapple supply tightness should support DMC's pricing (DMC is the largest pineapple marketer, and pineapple pricing drove its 2025 gross-profit increase). An exporter reported on 2026-04-17 that prices stayed more than 20% higher after annual programs closed, and the sector expected a supply gap of about 12 weeks after week 30 (late July-October), which falls inside DMC's Q3. The volume loss partly offsets the price.

findings.finding: On 2026-07-15 DMC upsized its revolver to $900M from $750M and removed the 10bp SOFR adjustment. Dec-31 trailing EBITDA = Q1 -8.3 + Q2 11.9 + Q3 + Q4. The low end of the FY guide ($78m) gives about 3.8-3.9x at ~$290-300m net debt, so a FY EBITDA guide cut of a few million or more at this print would put the Dec-31 test at or over 4.00x and imply another amendment. The guide line therefore carries covenant consequences on top of the usual guide-cut reaction, on a company that cut FY EBITDA from $105-120m (Feb) to $78-88m (Jul).
